title: Base change for open immersions
statement:
Let $K$ be a field. Let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion of
schemes of finite type over $K$ and let $Y$ be a scheme of finite
type over $K$. Consider the diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y\times_{\Spec(K)}X&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\times_{\Spec(K)}U\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle q}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}\\
X&\xleftarrow{\;j\;}&U .
\end{array}
$$

Then the exchange morphism of
[def-kun-unbounded-exchange],
$q^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rh_*p^{-1}F$, is an isomorphism for every abelian
sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$ whose stalks are torsion of orders
invertible in $K$. (*Source:* Stacks Project, Tag
[0F1H](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1H).)

proof.text: Write $Z=Y\times_KX$, $V=Y\times_KU$, and $\beta_F:q^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rh_*p^{-1}F$. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $K$. Thus $U,X,Y$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $j$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and clause (3) makes its base change $h$ so. We will also use those clauses for other indicated base changes. Inverse image for constant coefficients is exact and a left adjoint by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; it therefore preserves colimits, since maps out of the image of a colimit correspond under the adjunction to compatible maps out of its terms. For a sheaf in degree zero all our exchange maps lie in $D^+$: [lem-kun-unbounded-exchange-agrees] identifies the abelian unbounded map in the statement with the bounded-below map. The inclusion is full and faithful, so it reflects invertibility (an inverse and its two identities lift by fullness and faithfulness). By [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology] its degree-$r$ cohomology map is $q^{-1}R^rj_*F\to R^rh_*p^{-1}F$, and for $r<0$ both sides vanish. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] it is enough to prove these maps are isomorphisms for all $r\ge0$.

source.place: Tag 0F1H, lemma-kunneth-localize-on-X, first paragraph; geometric and derived-category hypotheses made explicit

proof.text: The stalk torsion hypothesis makes $F$ a locally torsion sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations], implication (3) to (2). By [lem-kun-invertible-orders-colimit], $F=\varinjlim_{n\in I_K}F[n]$, with $I_K$ the positive integers invertible in $K$, ordered by divisibility. This index is nonempty and directed: $1\in I_K$ and $nm$ is an upper bound for $n,m$. Each $F[n]$ has its canonical $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-module structure, since multiplication of sections by integers factors through this quotient. The stalk hypothesis on $F$ is exactly the invertible-order condition of [def-kun-torsion-invertible]. For fixed $r\ge0$, [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit] applies to $j,h$ from Step 1, and inverse images commute with colimits by Step 1. Naturality of exchange in its coefficient sheaf, as in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], identifies the degree-$r$ map for $F$ with the colimit of those for $F[n]$. A colimit of a natural family of isomorphisms is an isomorphism, since the compatible inverses induce its inverse. Hence it suffices to prove the assertion for sheaves annihilated by one $n\in I_K$. Such sheaves, and all inverse images of them, are still killed by $n$, so [lem-kun-zn-sheaf-invertible-orders] verifies every coefficient hypothesis below. No unbounded derived-colimit theorem is being inferred from a sheaf-colimit theorem.

source.place: Tag 0F1H, lemma-kunneth-localize-on-X, first paragraph, reduction to finite cyclic coefficients

proof.text: For all fields $K$ and all $n$ invertible in $K$ simultaneously, induct on $N=\dim X+\dim Y$ when $X,Y$ are nonempty; it is a nonnegative integer by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. If either factor is empty then $Z,V$ are empty and both objects are zero: an abelian sheaf on the empty scheme has only its zero section, by the empty-cover sheaf condition. Assume the assertion at all smaller sums. If $\dim X=0$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] makes $X$ finite discrete, so $U$ is open and closed. In the decomposition $X=U\amalg(X\setminus U)$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product] identifies restriction with projection onto the $U$ factor; its right adjoint $j_*$ inserts the zero sheaf on the other factor, because morphisms to that inserted object are precisely morphisms on $U$. Kernels and cokernels are componentwise in a product, so this insertion is exact. The same reasoning holds for $h$, which is again open and closed after base change. Consequently their higher direct images in positive degrees vanish, while degree zero exchange is an isomorphism by [lem-kun-base-change-open-closed]. Step 1 finishes this case. This includes the base $N=0$; the remaining argument is the induction step with $\dim X>0$.

source.place: Tag 0F1H, lemma-kunneth-localize-on-X, second paragraph, simultaneous induction and the open-and-closed base case

proof.text: The problem is local on the two factors. An open immersion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]; its base changes remain open immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. For an affine open $X_0\subset X$, use [lem-kun-0f09] with the constant one-term smooth system $X_0\to X$, first for $j$ with coefficient $F$, then for $h$ with coefficient $p^{-1}F$ and the base change $Y\times_KX_0\to Z$. These maps are qcqs by Step 1's permanence facts. The comparison diagram in clause (2) of [lem-kun-bc-base-change] has both vertical maps invertible, so it identifies the restriction of $\beta_F$ with the exchange for $U\times_XX_0\to X_0$ and $Y$. For an affine open $Y_0\subset Y$, apply the same smooth comparison to $h$ along $Y_0\times_KX\to Z$. Clause (1) of [lem-kun-bc-base-change], with $u:Y_0\times_KX\to Z$ and original square $(j,h,q,p)$, then identifies the product exchange for $Y_0$ with $\operatorname{Ex}_{h,u}\circ u^{-1}\beta_F$, under inverse-image composition. Thus restriction detects a failure at any specified geometric point, by [lem-kun-stalk-faithful-derived]. Affine opens and their inverse images here remain finite type: on a finite-type affine chart the quasi-compact open has a finite cover by principal opens $\operatorname{Spec}A_f$, and $A_f$ is finitely generated over $K$ by adjoining $f^{-1}$ to generators of $A$. Dimension cannot increase on an open: closure in $X$ of a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets in the open is still strict, since intersection with the open recovers the chain. Therefore a restriction with smaller dimension sum is handled by induction, and otherwise we may use affine $X,Y$ of the same sum when analyzing any point.

source.place: Tag 0F1H, lemma-kunneth-localize-on-X, locality in the minimal-counterexample paragraph, expanded before stalk analysis

proof.text: Take affine $X,Y$ as in Step 4, a geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$ with image $x\in X$, and assume $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)>0$. Set $X'=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$, $U'=U\times_XX'$, and $r_Z:Y\times_KX'\to Z$. By [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] this is the inverse limit of a small cofiltered system of affine pointed etale neighborhoods of $\bar x$; it is an inverse limit, not a colimit of schemes. [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] permits a directed index. The transition maps are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. The neighborhood maps to $X$ are qcqs by Step 1 and smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Their base changes to $Z$ have affine transitions by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and their limit is $Y\times_KX'$ by [lem-kun-fibre-product-limits]. Apply [lem-kun-0f09] to $j$ with $F$, and to $h$ with $p^{-1}F$; it yields canonical comparison isomorphisms $a:r_X^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rj'_*F'$ and $b:r_Z^{-1}Rh_*p^{-1}F\to Rh'_*p'^{-1}F'$. Here primes denote the product square over $X'$ and $F'=F|_{U'}$. Clause (2) of [lem-kun-bc-base-change] gives $b\circ r_Z^{-1}\beta_F=\beta_{F'}\circ q'^{-1}a$, after its specified inverse-image composition isomorphisms. Notice that the first direct-image leg is $j$, not $q$. The chosen $\bar z$ lifts to $Y\times_KX'$ by the pointed strict-localization map $\bar x\to X'$ and the fibre-product universal property. By [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], proving $\beta_{F'}$ invertible will therefore prove invertibility at $\bar z$.

source.place: Tag 0F1H, lemma-kunneth-localize-on-X, third paragraph, first strict-local comparison, with the correct direct-image legs

proof.text: By [lem-kun-0f0u], write $X'=\varprojlim_iX_i$ with affine finite-type $L$-schemes $X_i$, affine transitions, $L/K$ separably closed, and $\dim X_i<\dim X$. Reindex by a directed set as above if necessary. The open $U'\subset X'$ is quasi-compact since $j'$ is a qc base change of $j$. [lem-kun-descent-limit-open] gives a stage $i_0$ and a quasi-compact open $U_{i_0}\subset X_{i_0}$ inducing $U'$. For $i\ge i_0$ put $U_i=U_{i_0}\times_{X_{i_0}}X_i$ and $j_i:U_i\to X_i$; transitions are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and $U'=\varprojlim U_i$ by [lem-kun-fibre-product-limits]. Each $U_i$ is finite type over $L$ by the principal-open argument of Step 4. To reconstruct coefficients without assuming $U'$ affine, put $G=j'_*F'$ on the affine scheme $X'$, $G_i=\pi_{i,*}G$, and $F_i=j_i^{-1}G_i$. These sheaves are annihilated by $n$, as seen sectionwise for direct images and by additivity for inverse images. [lem-kun-descent-limit] applies on $X'$ to give $G=\varinjlim_i\pi_i^{-1}G_i$. Restrict this equality to $U'$ using the colimit-preserving inverse image of Step 1; the counit isomorphism of [lem-kun-open-immersion-restriction] gives $F'=\varinjlim_i(\pi_i|_{U'})^{-1}F_i$. The transition maps are the canonical ones from this reconstruction and remain compatible after restriction. Apply the induction hypothesis over $L$ to $j_i$, $Y_L$, and $F_i$: [lem-kun-dimension-extension] gives $\dim Y_L=\dim Y$, so each sum is smaller. For each $r\ge0$, [lem-kun-0ezt] now applies with its corners $(X_i,Y_i,S_i,T_i)=(Y_L\times_LX_i,Y_L\times_LU_i,X_i,U_i)$ and coefficient $F_i$ on $T_i=U_i$; its direct-image leg is $g_i=j_i$, which is qcqs. All transitions are affine, all limits have just been identified, and its limit coefficient is precisely $F'$. Thus every degree-$r$ exchange is invertible at the limit. Step 1 proves $\beta_{F'}$ invertible, completing the case of Step 5.

source.place: Tag 0F1H, lemma-kunneth-localize-on-X, third paragraph, smaller-dimensional affine models and coefficient reconstruction

proof.text: If instead $\bar z$ maps to $y\in Y$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(y)>0$, put $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$. The construction of Step 5, now using neighborhoods over $Y$, makes $f:Y'\times_KX\to Z$ a limit of smooth qcqs maps with affine transitions. Apply [lem-kun-0f09] to $h$ and $p^{-1}F$; clause (1) of [lem-kun-bc-base-change] identifies the exchange for the outer product square over $X$ with $\operatorname{Ex}_{h,f}\circ f^{-1}\beta_F$. By [lem-kun-0f0u], $Y'=\varprojlim_iY_i$ with affine finite-type schemes over a separably closed extension $L/K$ and $\dim Y_i<\dim Y$. The identifications $Y'\times_KX=Y'\times_LX_L$ and similarly for $U$ follow directly from the fibre-product universal properties. Apply the canonical field-extension exchange theorem [lem-kun-0f1c-exchange] to $j,F,L/K$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 1 and $nF=0$, and it gives an isomorphism $a:r_X^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rj_{L,*}F_L$. With $q':Y'\times_LX_L\to X_L$, clause (1) of [lem-kun-bc-base-change], this time factoring the outer base map as $r_Xq'$, gives $\beta_{\mathrm{outer}}=\beta'\circ q'^{-1}a$. Consequently it suffices to prove $\beta'$ invertible. For each $i$, induction applies over $L$ to $j_L$, $Y_i$, and $F_L$, because $\dim X_L=\dim X$ by [lem-kun-dimension-extension]. Apply [lem-kun-0ezt] degreewise with corners $(Y_i\times_LX_L,Y_i\times_LU_L,X_L,U_L)$; the two bottom systems and coefficient $F_L$ are constant, the direct-image leg is $j_L$, and the limit square follows from [lem-kun-fibre-product-limits]. This proves $\beta'$ invertible by Step 1. Pull back to the geometric lift of $\bar z$ as in Step 5 to conclude. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field] and [lem-kun-closed-points-of-product], every nonclosed point of $Z$ has at least one of these two positive-transcendence-degree images. Together with Step 4, we have proved invertibility at all nonclosed points for all data of dimension sum $N$, over every field.

source.place: Tag 0F1H, lemma-kunneth-localize-on-X, fourth paragraph, the second-factor case and the explicit two exchange factorizations

proof.text: Suppose a counterexample of sum $N$ remains. Step 7 makes its failures closed-point failures, and Step 4 allows an affine neighborhood in each factor retaining a failure; a smaller resulting sum is impossible by induction. For affine $Y$, [lem-kun-compactification-affine] gives an open dense embedding $Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ with $\overline Y$ projective over $K$, and [lem-kun-dimension-extension] gives $\dim\overline Y=\dim Y$. Step 4's open-restriction comparison in the second factor identifies the original map with the restriction of the map for $\overline Y$. Thus the latter is still a counterexample with the same sum. It suffices to rule out this projective case. By [lem-kun-0f1h-sep-reduction], it suffices to prove its scalar-extended map over $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ invertible. Dimension is unchanged by [lem-kun-dimension-extension]. Projectivity is unchanged by scalar extension by [lem-pc-projective-base-change]. Step 7 applies to this new data over the extended field and again gives invertibility at all nonclosed points. This last application is needed: no claim that arbitrary scalar extension carries the old closed support to closed support is being used. We may now work over separably closed $K$ with projective $Y$ and a map invertible at every nonclosed point.

source.place: Tag 0F1H, lemma-kunneth-localize-on-X, minimal-counterexample paragraph and beginning of the projective-case paragraph

proof.text:
Put $A=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ and retain the canonical $A$-module structure on $F$. Form the $A$-coefficient exchange $\beta_A$. By [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison], forgetting coefficients is exact and conservative, commutes with inverse/direct images by its endpoint isomorphisms, and carries $\beta_A$ to the original abelian exchange. Thus it is enough to prove $\beta_A$ invertible. The projective factor $Y$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. Apply [lem-kun-0f14b] to the ordered pairs $(Y,X)$ with $(\underline A_Y,Rj_*F)$ and $(Y,U)$ with $(\underline A_Y,F)$. In the notation of [lem-kun-bc-kunneth-compat], these give $k_Z$ and $k_W$, and that node supplies the canonical module-valued Leray isomorphisms $\lambda_j,\lambda_h$ and the precise equation
$$\lambda_h\,R\Gamma(Z,\beta_A)\,k_Z=k_W(1\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\lambda_j).$$
Every map on the right is invertible: tensoring an isomorphism sends its inverse to an inverse. Hence $R\Gamma(Z,\beta_A)$ is invertible. This uses the canonical exchange compatibility, not merely isomorphisms between the two cohomology objects.

source.place: Tag 0F1H, lemma-kunneth-localize-on-X, projective case, the two Kunneth isomorphisms and their compatibility with the actual exchange

proof.text: Complete $\beta_A$ to a distinguished triangle $q^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rh_*p^{-1}F\to Q_A\to(q^{-1}Rj_*F)[1]$. Its endpoints are bounded below, so $Q_A$ is bounded below too, by the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. Let $Q$ be its underlying abelian derived object. Exactness and cohomology compatibility of [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison], together with exact inverse image from Step 1, identify $Q$ with a cone of $\beta_F$ and identify its geometric stalks with the cones of the stalk maps. Hence Step 7 gives $Q_{\bar z}=0$ at every nonclosed point. Derived global sections preserve distinguished triangles by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] applied to the additive global-sections functor. Step 9 and the long exact sequence therefore give $H^r(Z,Q_A)=0$ for every $r$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-underlying-comparison] to the bounded-below coefficient complex $Q_A$, base $T=Z$, and $p=\mathrm{id}_Z$: it identifies the underlying abelian group of $H^r(Z,Q_A)$ with $H^r(Z,Q)$, so the latter is zero for every $r$ as well. The scheme $Z$ is finite type over the separably closed field $K$: by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], products of finite-type affine charts have tensor-product coordinate rings, generated over $K$ by the images of the two finite sets of generators, and these charts form a finite cover. All hypotheses of [lem-kun-0f1g] now hold, so $Q=0$. The long exact sequence and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] make $\beta_F$ invertible. By the conservative coefficient comparison $\beta_A$ is also invertible. This contradicts the projective counterexample, completes the induction, and Step 2 proves the assertion for the original sheaf without a uniform annihilator.

source.place: Tag 0F1H, lemma-kunneth-localize-on-X, projective case, closed-point-supported cone and global cohomology detection

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $K$ be a field. Let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion of
schemes of finite type over $K$ and let $Y$ be a scheme of finite
type over $K$. Consider the diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y\times_{\Spec(K)}X&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\times_{\Spec(K)}U\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle q}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}\\
X&\xleftarrow{\;j\;}&U .
\end{array}
$$

Then the exchange morphism of
[def-kun-unbounded-exchange],
$q^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rh_*p^{-1}F$, is an isomorphism for every abelian
sheaf $F$ on $U_{\Et}$ whose stalks are torsion of orders
invertible in $K$.

proof.text:
*Reduction to $\kunZn$-coefficients.* Write $F=\varinjlim F[n]$ where the colimit is over the multiplicative system of integers
invertible in $K$ ([def-kun-torsion-invertible] and
[lem-kun-invertible-orders-colimit]). Both sides
of the exchange morphism of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] commute
with filtered colimits in $F$: $Rj_*$ and $Rh_*$ by the
sheaf-level filtered-colimit property of
[lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit] in each degree
(together with the truncation triangles of
[def-kun-truncations]), and the inverse images are exact.
Hence it suffices to prove the lemma for each $F[n]$, a sheaf of
$\kunZn$-modules which has orders invertible in $K$ by
[lem-kun-zn-sheaf-invertible-orders]; that is, we may assume that
$F$ is a sheaf of $\kunZn$-modules for some $n$ invertible in
$K$.

*Induction.* We prove the lemma by induction on
$\kundim X+\kundim Y$, finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], (well-founded induction on the pair of
dimensions). If $\kundim X\le0$, then $X$ is a finite discrete
set of points ([lem-kun-finite-closed-subscheme]: every
irreducible component of $X$ is a point, hence closed), so $U$ is
open and closed in $X$, and the claim follows from
[lem-kun-base-change-open-closed]. This covers the base of the
induction.

*Stalks over points with positive transcendence degree.*
Choose a point $z\in X\times_KY$; we will show that the exchange
morphism is an isomorphism on the stalk at every geometric point
$\bar z$ over $z$ ([lem-kun-stalk-faithful-derived]).

Suppose first that $z$ maps to $x\in X$ with
$\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)>0$. Set
$X'=\Spec(\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,x})$ and denote
$U'\subset X'$ the inverse image of $U$. Consider the base change

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y\times_KX'&\xleftarrow{\;h'\;}&Y\times_KU'\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle q'}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p'}\\
X'&\xleftarrow{\;j'\;}&U'
\end{array}
$$

of our diagram by $X'\to X$. The morphism $X'\to X$ is a filtered
colimit of etale (in particular smooth) morphisms
([def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]), so by smooth base
change in the form of [lem-kun-0f09] applied to
$q:Y\times_KX\to X$ with $E:=Rj_*F$, and to
$h:Y\times_KU\to Y\times_KX$ with $E:=p^{-1}F$ (both
$E$ lie in $\Dplus$ with stalks of torsion orders invertible on
the base), the pullback of the exchange morphism to
$Y\times_KX'$ is, by [lem-kun-bc-base-change], the exchange
morphism
$(q')^{-1}Rj'_*F'\to Rh'_*(p')^{-1}F'$, where $F'$ is the pullback
of $F$ to $U'$. So it suffices to show that the latter map is an
isomorphism, for then the original map is an isomorphism on stalks at
$\bar z$ (stalks are computed by pullback,
[lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback]).

By [lem-kun-0f0u] there is a separably closed field $L/K$ such
that $X'=\varprojlim_iX_i$ with $X_i$ affine of finite type over
$L$ and $\kundim X_i<\kundim X$ (using
$\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)>0$). For $i$ large enough there
exists an open $U_i\subset X_i$ restricting to $U'$ in $X'$
([lem-kun-descent-limit-open]), and the sheaf $F'$ is a
filtered colimit of pullbacks of sheaves on the $U_i$
([lem-kun-descent-limit]). We apply the induction hypothesis to
the diagrams

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y\times_KX_i&\xleftarrow{\;h_i\;}&Y\times_KU_i\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle q_i}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p_i}\\
X_i&\xleftarrow{\;j_i\;}&U_i
\end{array}
\qquad\text{equal to}\qquad
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y_L\times_LX_i&\xleftarrow{\;h_i\;}&Y_L\times_LU_i\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle q_i}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p_i}\\
X_i&\xleftarrow{\;j_i\;}&U_i
\end{array}
$$

over the field $L$ and to the pullbacks of $F$ to these diagrams:
here $\kundim X_i+\kundim Y_L<\kundim X+\kundim Y$ by
[lem-kun-dimension-extension], so the induction hypothesis
applies and the exchange morphisms at the finite levels are isomorphisms. By [lem-kun-0ezt], applied to the affine limit
system $X_i$, we conclude that the map
$(q')^{-1}Rj'_*F'\to Rh'_*(p')^{-1}F'$ is an isomorphism.

Suppose now that $z$ maps to $y\in Y$ with
$\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(y)>0$. Let
$Y'=\Spec(\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,y})$. By
[lem-kun-0f0u] there is a separably closed field $L/K$ with
$Y'=\varprojlim_iY_i$, $Y_i$ affine of finite type over $L$ and
$\kundim Y_i<\kundim Y$; in particular $Y'$ is a scheme over $L$.
Denote with a subscript $L$ base change from schemes over $K$ to
schemes over $L$. Consider the commutative diagrams

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
Y'\times_KX&\xleftarrow{\;h'\;}&Y'\times_KU\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f'}\\
Y\times_KX&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\times_KU\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle q}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}\\
X&\xleftarrow{\;j\;}&U
\end{array}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\begin{array}{ccccc}
Y'\times_LX_L&\xleftarrow{\;h'\;}&Y'\times_LU_L\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle q'}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p'}\\
X_L&\xleftarrow{\;j_L\;}&U_L\\
\Big\downarrow{}&&\Big\downarrow{}\\
X&\xleftarrow{\;j\;}&U
\end{array}
$$

and observe that the top rows are the same on the left and on the
right (canonical identifications of fibre products,
[lem-kun-fibre-product-limits]). By smooth base change
([lem-kun-0f09], applied to the square
$Y'\times_KU\to Y'\times_KX$ over $Y'\to Y$) we see that
$f^{-1}Rh_*p^{-1}F=Rh'_*(f')^{-1}p^{-1}F$. By smooth base change
for $\Spec(L)\to\Spec(K)$ in the form of [lem-kun-0f1c] we see that $Rj_{L,*}F_L$ is the pullback of $Rj_*F$ to $X_L$.
Combining these two observations, and using that a vertical
composition of exchange morphisms is an exchange morphism
([lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting]) we conclude that it suffices to prove that the
exchange morphism for the upper square in the second diagram is an
isomorphism, in order to prove that our original map is an
isomorphism on stalks at $\bar z$. Then, using that
$Y'=\varprojlim_iY_i$ and arguing exactly as in the previous
paragraph ([lem-kun-descent-limit],
[lem-kun-descent-limit-open], the induction hypothesis – since
$\kundim X_L+\kundim Y_i<\kundim X+\kundim Y$ by
[lem-kun-dimension-extension] – and [lem-kun-0ezt]), we
see that the induction hypothesis forces our map over
$Y'\times_KX$ to be an isomorphism.

*Minimal counterexample.* Thus any counterexample with
$\kundim X+\kundim Y$ minimal would have the exchange morphism an
isomorphism on all stalks at non-closed points of $X\times_KY$,
because by [lem-kun-closed-points-of-product] a point $z$ of
$X\times_KY$ is closed if and only if both of its images in $X$
and $Y$ are closed. Since it is enough to prove the isomorphism
after base change along open immersions of the factors
([lem-kun-stalk-faithful-derived]; the base change along the
open immersions $X_0\to X$, $Y_0\to Y$ is a smooth base change
applied to the exchang morphism by [lem-kun-0f09] and
[lem-kun-bc-base-change]), we may assume $X$ and $Y$ are
affine, after replacing them by affine open neighbourhoods of the
images of a closed point where the map is not an isomorphism; the dimension sum cannot increase. However, then we can choose a dense open immersion $Y\to Y'$ with $Y'$ projective over $K$
([lem-kun-compactification-affine]); we have
$\kundim Y'=\kundim Y$ ([lem-kun-dimension-extension]), so we
get a minimal counterexample with $Y$ projective over $K$ (and
with the exchange morphism an isomorphism at all non-closed points).
In the next paragraph we show that this cannot happen.

*The projective case.* Consider a diagram as in the statement
of the lemma such that
$q^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rh_*p^{-1}F$ is an isomorphism at all non-closed
points of $X\times_KY$ and such that $Y$ is projective over $K$.
The restriction of the map to $(X\times_KY)_{K^{\mathrm{sep}}}$ is
the corresponding map for the diagram of the lemma base changed to
$K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ ([lem-kun-0f1c] and
[lem-kun-bc-base-change]), so by
[lem-kun-0f1h-sep-reduction] we may and do assume $K$ is
separably closed. Choose a distinguished triangle

$$
q^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rh_*p^{-1}F\to Q\to(q^{-1}Rj_*F)[1]
$$

in $D((X\times_KY)_{\Et})$. Since the first map is an isomorphism
on stalks at all non-closed points, $Q$ has nonzero stalks only at
closed points of $X\times_KY$, so by [lem-kun-0f1g] it
suffices to prove $H^i((X\times_KY)_{\Et},Q)=0$ for all $i$.
Thus it suffices to prove that
$q^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rh_*p^{-1}F$ induces an isomorphism on cohomology.
Recall that $F$ is annihilated by $n$ invertible in $K$. By the
Kunneth formula of [lem-kun-0f14b] (with proper factor $Y$,
which is projective hence proper by
[lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] and
[lem-kun-proper-stability], and $E=\underline{\kunZn}$; here
$Rj_*F\in D(X_{\Et},\kunZn)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_KY)_{\Et},q^{-1}Rj_*F\bigr)
&\cong\RGamma(X_{\Et},Rj_*F)\kunotimes{\kunZn}
\RGamma(Y_{\Et},\underline{\kunZn})\\
&\cong\RGamma(U_{\Et},F)\kunotimes{\kunZn}
\RGamma(Y_{\Et},\underline{\kunZn}),
\end{aligned}
$$

using [lem-kun-tensor-unit]
for $q^{-1}Rj_*F\cong\pr_1^{-1}\underline{\kunZn}\kunotimes{\kunZn} \pr_2^{-1}Rj_*F$ and [lem-kun-leray-bdd]
for the second line, and

$$
\RGamma\bigl((X\times_KY)_{\Et},Rh_*p^{-1}F\bigr)
\cong\RGamma\bigl((U\times_KY)_{\Et},p^{-1}F\bigr)
\cong\RGamma(U_{\Et},F)\kunotimes{\kunZn}
\RGamma(Y_{\Et},\underline{\kunZn})
$$

(using [lem-kun-leray-bdd] for $h$ and
[lem-kun-0f14b] for the pair $(Y,U)$). By
[lem-kun-bc-kunneth-compat], $\RGamma$ of the exchange
morphism is, under these identifications, the identity, hence an
isomorphism. This finishes the proof.
